subject: general
question: What similarities do plastids share with mitochondria?

options.text: Both contain their own DNA and ribosomes.
Both are present only in plant cells.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both contain their own DNA and ribosomes.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Autonomous DNA:** Both plastids and mitochondria contain their own genetic material, separate from the nuclear DNA of the cell.
 
• **Presence of Ribosomes:** Both organelles have their own ribosomes, enabling them to produce some of their own proteins.
 
• **Endosymbiotic Origin:** Both plastids and mitochondria are believed to have originated from ancient endosymbiotic bacteria.
 
• **Double Membrane Structure:** Both organelles are enclosed by a double membrane, which is indicative of their complex origin and functional specialization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts:** A type of plastid that contains chlorophyll and is involved in photosynthesis in plant cells.
 
• **ATP Production:** Mitochondria are the main sites of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) production through cellular respiration in eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Photosynthesis:** Plastids such as chloroplasts are involved in photosynthesis, converting light energy into chemical energy in the form of glucose.
 
• **Cellular Respiration:** Mitochondria play a crucial role in cellular respiration, where glucose is broken down to produce ATP, the energy currency of the cell.
